description: All three workers converged on the same wall: the dense shapes need a FAST BATCHED TENSOR-CORE small-eigh PRIMITIVE (the O(n^3) inner eigh is 99% of cost; filter/split GEMMs are cheap). Build it by extending the proven n<=200 fused FP16 SMEM-resident megakernel to medium n (256-512): one CTA per matrix, SMEM-TILE the matrix and WARP-SPECIALIZE (sm_100 tcgen05 MMA producers + Jacobi/Householder consumers) so the n^2 working set that overflows 228KB SMEM at n>=352 is streamed in tiles, keeping all stages (reduction + eigenvectors + back-transform) fused with no HBM round-trips. Direct win on n=352 (shape2, 21150us, now cuSOLVER) AND the fast leaf brief-0's sign-split feeds (split 512->256 leaves). Per-matrix residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback; route via the existing router. Verdict = full 13-shape geomean < 47824 + 39/39.

medium-n fused megakernel (packed FP16 lower-tri A in SMEM + global eigenvector matrix), NT=1024. Extends the n<=200 megakernel to n=256-448, breaking the 228KB SMEM cliff. Root-caused trial2 regression: NT=768 produces garbage (red[] pow2 tree reduction bug) -> 100% fallback; NT must be pow2. ncu: kernel latency-bound (3.2% SM, 12.5% occ), more warps hide latency. Shape2 n=352 b40: 20111->17509us (1.15x faster). Geomean 48704->47392us. Validated 39/39. n=256 tie, n=448 0.91x.
[retro-logged, trial 1] medium-n kernel NT=256: validated 39/39, n=352 27754us (1.38x SLOWER than cuSOLVER 20111). ncu showed latency-bound at 12.5% occupancy. Geomean 49241.
[retro-logged, trial 2] medium-n kernel NT=768: BROKEN (non-pow2 red[] reduction bug) -> 100% cuSOLVER fallback, n=352 37871us. Geomean 49860. Led to the pow2 diagnosis.

SMEM-column-blocked BARRIER-FREE back-transform. Stage-split profiling: back-transform was 78% of kernel (n=448 b640 158ms) / 72% (n=352). Reflectors on one column are independent across columns -> one thread owns a column across ALL reflectors: no inter-reflector barrier, V in SMEM (column-blocked, post-reduction free A region). Global V traffic 2n^3->~2n^2*(n/BV). Shape2 n=352 17509->15200us (1.32x vs baseline). Geomean 47392->46669us. Kernel 26.96ms(t1)->14.5ms. Validated 39/39, 0 fallback.

BLOCKED COMPACT-WY back-transform via cooperative SMEM GEMMs. Per-column-serial sweep left only BV<<nt threads active; panel-blocked WY Q_blk-=Y(T(Y^T Q_blk)) engages ALL nt threads, ~n/NB barriers. V in column blocks (post-reduction free SMEM) + panel Y + Gram->block-T (one warp, shfl) + Z/Z2. Reverse panel order. Fixed shfl_sync deadlock + block-T lower-zero bug. Shape2 n=352 15200->13142us (1.53x vs baseline). Geomean 46669->46132us. n=256 1.12x n=448 0.99x. Validated 39/39, 0 fallback.

Tune blocked-WY panel NB 32->16 (swept 8/16/24/32; 16 fastest: smaller panel -> larger V column block fits SMEM + more GEMM parallelism; NB<=32 for one-warp block-T). Shape2 n=352 13142->10840us (1.86x vs baseline). Geomean 46132->45489us. Validated 39/39.

Raise medium-route cap 400->448. Fast blocked-WY back-transform makes the kernel win the whole SMEM-fit range at both batch sizes (b640 n=384 1.53x/n=416 1.77x/n=448 1.70x; b40 up to 1.86x). Routes all (200,448]; gate falls unresolved matrices. Geomean 45475us (==trial6, no benchmark shape in 400-448). Idle-verified, 39/39.

MEDIUM-n fused megakernel BUILT, validated, banked. HEAD 9d38abc2a, geomean 48704->45475us idle-verified (~6.6%; ~5% vs parent 47824), 39/39 PASS, 0 fallback. Single moved shape: SHAPE 2 (n=352 b40) 20111->10849us = 1.85x. All other 12 shapes identical (cuSOLVER floor).

WHAT WORKED (7 trials): extended the n<=200 megakernel to n=256-448 by (a) PACKED FP16 LOWER-TRIANGLE A in SMEM (symmetric -> half the bytes, fits n<=448 @200KB vs n<=320 full) + (b) eigenvector matrix V in GLOBAL (n^2 FP32 can't be SMEM-resident at medium n). Three levers, each measured: (1) NT 256->1024 [non-pow2 NT=768 produced GARBAGE via the red[] tree-reduction dropping elements -> 100% fallback; NT must be pow2]; raised n=352 to 1.15x. (2) The BACK-TRANSFORM is the dominant stage (stage-split: 78% at n=448 b640 / 72% at n=352) -- it applied each Householder reflector to GLOBAL V with a __syncthreads per reflector + 2n^3 traffic. Rewrote it as BLOCKED COMPACT-WY via cooperative SMEM GEMMs (Q_blk -= Y(T(Y^T Q_blk)), panel NB=16, block-T built by one warp via shfl, V in column-blocks in the post-reduction-free SMEM, panels reverse order): engages ALL nt threads, ~n/NB barriers. n=352 1.15x->1.86x. (3) cap raised to 448: the fast back-transform moved the crossover up so the kernel now WINS the WHOLE fit range at full occupancy -- MEASURED b640: n=384 1.53x, n=416 1.77x, n=448 1.70x; b40 up to 1.86x. Kernel 26.96ms(t1)->10.18ms(t7) at n=352.

n=512 (the 4 biggest shapes, 165-204ms each) MEASURED OUT OF REACH for one-CTA: (a) packed-FP16 reduction = 257KB > 232KB SMEM cap; (b) FP8-packed reduction (131KB, fits) is too inaccurate -> orth~19, 100% gate fallback; (c) GLOBAL-A tiled reduction ALONE = 292ms at n=512 b640 vs cuSOLVER's ENTIRE eigh 191ms (1.5x slower) -- the in-SMEM resident-matrix no-re-read advantage that makes the kernel win VANISHES when A doesn't fit. Extrapolated, IF n=512 fit in SMEM the kernel would be ~133ms vs cuSOLVER 172ms (~1.29x), so the win exists but the SMEM cliff blocks it.

OPEN DIRECTIONS for the manager (not closed): (1) TENSOR-CORE (WMMA/tcgen05) for the back-transform GEMMs -- they are currently FP32 SIMT (the kernel is now 95% SM-compute-bound, not memory); FP16-MMA could cut the back-transform (~55% of the kernel) ~3-5x, est ~2.8x on n=352, BUT FP16 orthogonality error (~1e-2) exceeds the n=352 gate (5.3e-3) so it needs an FP32 Newton-Schulz cleanup -- unbuilt, accuracy-vs-speed tradeoff to measure. (2) The medium kernel IS the fast D&C LEAF the brief's payoff-2 wants: it wins n=256 1.12x / n=320 1.05x / n=128 even better -- a spectral split of n=512->2x256 with these leaves (brief-0 territory; brief-0 plateaued because its leaves were slow cuSOLVER/old-megakernel, NOT these). (3) BLOCKED tensor-core reduction (panel WY trailing update A-=VW^T+WV^T as MMA) to push the crossover past 448 -- but the n=512 SMEM cliff still blocks resident A. (4) reduction is now 40% of the kernel (packed-FP16 SIMT symv with a branchy AGET) -- a symmetric-matvec (touch each lower element once) could ~halve the symv. (5) n=448 b640 orth=4.9e-3 sits just under the 5.3e-3 gate; a reseed could tip it -> the gate falls it to cuSOLVER (safe, no regression) but worth a tighter reduction for robustness.

Re-entry pursued manager lanes #1 (tensor-core back-transform) and #2 (n=512 tensor-core tiled reduction). Both BUILT and MEASURED; both do NOT beat the current state. HEAD stays at trial-7 9d38abc2a (banked best: geomean 45475, n=352 1.86x, 39/39). No new committed trial -- both probes measured no improvement over the live path, so committing either would regress the geomean.

#1 WMMA BACK-TRANSFORM -- BUILT (standalone, compiles -arch=sm_100a), CORRECT, but NOT FASTER. Full FP16 m16n16k16 WMMA for all 3 cooperative GEMMs (Z=Y^T@Vblk, Z2=T@Z, Vblk-=Y@Z2 via acc-init=Vblk + negated-Y so the subtract is one mma_sync), block-T built by one warp via shfl. Accuracy CONFIRMED PASS: FP16-WMMA + 2 FP32 Newton-Schulz iters -> orth 5e-6 (gate 5e-3), eig 1.4e-3 (gate 1e-2) at n=256/352/448. SPEED (CW swept 32/64/128, best CW=64): n=352 b40 6003us vs the tuned SIMT cooperative GEMM ~5500us (SLIGHTLY SLOWER); n=448 b640 59063us (SIMT ~comparable/faster). ROOT CAUSE: the back-transform is sequential over reflector panels, so Vblk must be re-cast FP32->FP16 EVERY panel (n/16 times) -- this cast + SMEM data movement dominates, and the MMA compute was never the bottleneck (ncu's '95% compute-bound' was SIMT-FMA throughput, but swapping FMA->MMA just shifts the bound to the casts). Tensor cores don't help a cast/movement-bound kernel.

#2 n=512 TILED TENSOR-CORE REDUCTION -- the SYMV BANDWIDTH FLOOR kills it. Measured the reduction's level-2 symv work ALONE (n-1 sequential p=A_trailing@v passes, A in global FP16, one CTA/matrix, NO rank-2 update/solve/back-transform): n=512 b640 = 119665us = 70% of cuSOLVER's ENTIRE eigh (172000us); n=448 = 81407us. The symv is matrix-VECTOR (batched over a panel it's a GEMM, but the per-column Householder dependency serializes it), and tensor cores accelerate COMPUTE not the global re-reads of the non-resident trailing matrix. Even a perfect tensor-core syr2k trailing update leaves this ~120ms symv floor + solve(~20ms) + back-transform(~40ms) = ~180ms+ > cuSOLVER 172ms. Corroborates brief-1's MEASURED tensor-core two-stage reduction at 553ms (dense->band 187ms + band->tridiag 366ms). cuSOLVER wins n=512 because per-matrix sytrd keeps the trailing matrix in on-chip memory using the WHOLE GPU per matrix; one-CTA-per-matrix re-reads it from global.

#3 D&C-LEAF split: dense no-gap spectra can't be cheaply split (briefs 0 & 2 measured: sign/Chebyshev can't separate +/-lam degeneracy; block-Jacobi rotation-generation is recursive small-eigh = 24s). Not pursued (off the megakernel line, and the cheap-split precondition fails for the dense benchmark shapes).

WHAT IS STILL OPEN: (a) shape 8 (n=512 b640 RANKDEF, rank=3n/4=384) and possibly shape 12-like CONCENTRATED n=512 shapes have exploitable LOW-RANK structure -- the existing _eigh_lowrank_safe path (wins n=1024 geometric 1.748x) might extend to n=512 rankdef; this is a structured-routing/combine lever, NOT the dense megakernel. (b) A properly BLOCKED tensor-core latrd reduction (panel symv batched as one A@V_panel GEMM + syr2k trailing update, the level-3 formulation) has a theoretical ~7ms bandwidth floor but brief-1 measured 553ms building it -- the 80x theory-vs-measured gap means it's a hard dedicated-kernel effort (brief-1's line, not megakernel-extension). (c) the banked n=352 1.86x kernel: reduction is now 40% (packed-FP16 SIMT symv, branchy AGET); a symmetric-matvec touching each lower element once could ~halve it. The medium kernel WINS the whole n in (200,448] range (b640: 1.53-1.77x) and IS the validated fast D&C leaf if a cheap split is ever found for structured inputs.
